sections.content: Long Beach, California sits at a fascinating crossroads. It's one of the largest cities in Los Angeles County, home to a major international port, a booming downtown, and neighborhoods ranging from beachfront luxury to distressed urban pockets ripe for investment. For investors who know where to look, real estate deals in Long Beach CA can generate strong returns through wholesaling, flipping, or buy-and-hold rentals. Whether you're a seasoned investor or just getting started — check out this [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first — Long Beach deserves a serious look in 2024.
Long Beach CA Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Long Beach is a city of about 460,000 people spread across 50 square miles. It borders Los Angeles to the north, Orange County to the east, and the Pacific Ocean to the south. That geographic diversity drives a wide range of property values and investment opportunities within a single city. The Port of Long Beach is the second-busiest container port in the United States, anchoring a strong local economy built on logistics, healthcare, aerospace, and a growing tech sector. This economic diversity means the city doesn't boom and bust on a single industry, which gives investors a more stable foundation than many California markets.
Average Home Prices in Long Beach CA

As of late 2024, the median home price in Long Beach sits around $750,000 to $800,000 — well below the broader Los Angeles County median of roughly $900,000. That discount is one reason investors keep coming back. However, prices vary dramatically by neighborhood. Homes in Belmont Shore or Naples Island can push $1.2 million or more, while properties in North Long Beach or Central Long Beach can still be found in the $500,000 to $650,000 range. For investors focused on distressed assets and wholesale deals, that lower end of the market is where the action is. Average price per square foot citywide runs between $480 and $580, with newer or fully renovated properties in desirable zip codes pushing significantly higher.

Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Long Beach
North Long Beach: The Highest Upside Pocket

North Long Beach — especially the zip codes 90805 and 90806 — is where many experienced investors focus their energy. Properties here are priced 20 to 30 percent below the city median, vacancy rates are higher than other areas, and there is a solid population of motivated sellers. The neighborhood has seen significant city investment in recent years, with infrastructure improvements and new commercial development signaling a long-term trajectory upward. For wholesalers and flippers, North Long Beach offers distressed inventory at prices that still leave room for a healthy margin.
Central Long Beach: Consistent Rental Demand

Central Long Beach, particularly around the 90806 and 90810 zip codes, offers strong rental demand driven by proximity to the port, major employers, and California State University Long Beach. Investors looking at buy-and-hold strategies find that two- and three-bedroom homes here rent for $2,200 to $2,800 per month, which can produce reasonable cash flow when purchased below market. Duplexes and small multifamily properties are especially valuable here for building long-term wealth.
Bixby Knolls: Value-Add Fix and Flip Opportunities

Bixby Knolls is an established, mid-city neighborhood with charming 1940s and 1950s bungalows and ranch-style homes. It has a strong owner-occupant base, which means flipped properties that are done well sell quickly. After-repair values in Bixby Knolls frequently reach $750,000 to $900,000 for updated three-bedroom homes, while distressed properties can still be acquired in the $550,000 to $650,000 range. The math works for experienced flippers willing to manage a full cosmetic or moderate structural renovation.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Long Beach

items: Wholesale Deals: Distressed single-family homes in North Long Beach and Central Long Beach with motivated sellers facing probate, divorce, or deferred maintenance situations. Assignment fees of $15,000 to $40,000 are achievable on well-sourced deals. Read our full guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the mechanics.

Fix and Flip: Cosmetic and light-structural flips in Bixby Knolls, Wrigley, and parts of East Long Beach. Typical renovation budgets run $60,000 to $120,000 with ARVs supporting a 20 to 25 percent gross margin on well-bought deals.

Buy and Hold Rentals: Multifamily properties — especially duplexes and triplexes — throughout Central and North Long Beach. California's strong tenant demand and persistent housing shortage support rent growth even in softer economic periods.

Short-Term Rentals: Beachside neighborhoods near Alamitos Beach and Belmont Shore attract Airbnb demand year-round, though local STR regulations require permits and compliance with city ordinances — always verify current rules before purchasing.
BRRRR Strategy: Buy distressed, renovate, refinance, rent, and repeat. Long Beach's consistent appreciation makes this a viable strategy for investors building a portfolio over time.

sections.content: Long Beach Real Estate Market Trends in 2024

The Long Beach market has cooled slightly from the frenzy of 2021 and 2022, but inventory remains historically tight. Homes that are priced correctly and in good condition still receive multiple offers, particularly below the $700,000 threshold. Days on market have extended from an average of 15 days in 2022 to closer to 35 to 45 days in late 2024, which actually helps investors who need more time to conduct due diligence. Interest rate pressure has pushed some would-be buyers back to renting, strengthening the landlord position in the market. For investors, the best opportunity window right now is distressed and off-market properties where sellers aren't competing for attention. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is the single most valuable skill you can develop in this market.
The best deals in any California market are never listed on the MLS. They're found through relationships, direct outreach, and showing up before anyone else knows the property is available.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Long Beach

Long Beach attracts significant interest from out-of-state investors, particularly from Texas, Arizona, and the Pacific Northwest, looking to gain exposure to the California market without paying the premium prices of Beverly Hills or Santa Monica. The city's relatively accessible price points and strong rental fundamentals make it attractive, but remote investing requires more preparation than buying in your backyard. Here's what you need to know before you make your first move.

items: Build a local team first: You need a property manager, a general contractor, a real estate attorney familiar with California landlord-tenant law, and ideally a boots-on-the-ground wholesaler or agent. Do not buy without this team in place.

Understand California's landlord-tenant laws: California is a highly tenant-protective state. Security deposit rules, eviction timelines, and habitability standards are stricter than most other states. Factor this into your cash flow projections.

Use technology to analyze deals remotely: Tools like the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) let you run the numbers quickly from anywhere before committing to an in-person visit.

Visit before you close: Even with the best remote tools, walk every property before closing. Long Beach neighborhoods can change significantly from block to block, and photos don't tell the full story.

Target off-market and distressed inventory: Listed properties in Long Beach are highly competitive and rarely offer investor-level margins. Your edge as an out-of-state investor comes from sourcing deals others don't see. Study how to [analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) so you can move quickly and confidently when a deal appears.

Account for California's high transaction costs: Escrow fees, transfer taxes, and title costs in California run higher than the national average. Build an additional 1 to 1.5 percent of purchase price into your acquisition cost estimates.

Is Long Beach a Good Real Estate Investment in 2024?

The short answer is yes — for investors who buy correctly. Long Beach is not a market where you can overpay and hope appreciation bails you out. Margins are tight at full retail prices. But for investors who source deals below market value, understand the local neighborhood dynamics, and run disciplined numbers, the city offers a compelling combination of rental demand, appreciation potential, and deal variety that few Southern California markets can match. The port economy, the university, and the city's ongoing revitalization investments create a durable foundation that supports long-term holds. For flippers and wholesalers, the distressed inventory in North and Central Long Beach continues to generate opportunities that reward those willing to do the work of finding them.
